claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

is_adopting.description: Whether the claimant is adopting the child.

child_has_moved_in.description: Whether the child being adopted has come to live with the claimant.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'll be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I need to ask you a few questions.

First, do you have any children you'd like to claim Child Benefit for?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do. I'd like to claim for my child Alex, who is 11 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask you some questions.

Do you live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great. Now I need to ask: do you live with Alex, or if not, do you pay at least the same amount as Child Benefit (or the equivalent in kind) towards looking after Alex - for example on food, clothes or pocket money?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex doesn't live with me at the moment, but I do contribute towards their upkeep. I help out with things like clothes, school supplies, and other essentials - I give about £30 a week.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for that information. Can you tell me how long Alex has been living away from you? And who is Alex currently living with?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is living with their other parent right now. As for how long - well, we've been separated for a while now, so Alex has been living there for some time. The important thing is I'm still very much involved and contributing to their care.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I understand. To help determine your eligibility, I need to know: is the other parent currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or do you know if they are planning to claim?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, the other parent isn't claiming Child Benefit for Alex, and as far as I know, they're not planning to claim either.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for clarifying that. Just to confirm - when you say you contribute about £30 a week towards Alex's upkeep (for things like clothes, school supplies, and other essentials), have you been making these contributions regularly and consistently?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have been making these contributions regularly and consistently.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you. One more important question: Is Alex currently in hospital, care, or any residential accommodation, or do they simply live at home with their other parent?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex just lives at home with their other parent - nothing like hospital or care or anything like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good news! **You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:

✓ **Age requirement met**: Alex is 11 years old, which is under 16
✓ **UK residency**: You live in the UK
✓ **Responsibility for the child**: Even though Alex doesn't live with you, you're making regular and consistent contributions of £30 per week towards Alex's upkeep (clothes, school supplies, and essentials). This exceeds the Child Benefit payment amount, which means you meet the responsibility test
✓ **No conflict**: The other parent is not claiming Child Benefit for Alex

According to the rules, you'll usually be responsible for a child if you're paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit (or the equivalent in kind) towards looking after them. Your £30 weekly contribution satisfies this requirement.

**Important note**: Please be aware that if either you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may have to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge. You can use the Child Benefit tax calculator to work out if this applies to you.

You can proceed with your Child Benefit application for Alex.

Since only one person can claim Child Benefit for a child, and the claimant meets the responsibility test through their financial contributions, they are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.
